title: Severe MIH Teeth Held Up Into Adulthood, but Fear
html:
Between ages 16 and 27, teeth with severe molar-incisor hypomineralization showed no more caries, tooth loss, or endodontic treatment than unaffected teeth. Participants with severe MIH were, however, more likely to avoid dental care because of fear, according to a Norwegian longitudinal study published Nov. 12 in the European Archives of Paediatric Dentistry.

The study drew on 518 participants in the Fit Futures cohort who had dental data at ages 16 and 27. MIH was assessed at age 16 using standardized criteria. At that point, 54 teeth had severe MIH, 125 had mild MIH, and 7,492 had none.

Only one surface with severe MIH had dentin caries at 16, and none did at 27. Over the study period, teeth with severe MIH did not show higher levels of caries, tooth loss, or endodontic treatment than unaffected teeth.

Dental avoidance told a different story. At age 27, 20.0% of participants with severe MIH reported avoiding dental care because of fear, compared with 8.6% of those without severe MIH (P = .018).

Dental anxiety scores fell over time among participants with no or mild MIH, from a median of 7.0 at 16 to 6.0 at 27 (P < .001). They did not fall among those with severe MIH, whose median moved from 7.0 to 7.5 (P = .829). After adjustment for sex and education, severe MIH was not significantly associated with oral health-related quality of life or with dental anxiety scores at 27.

The study was conducted by E. Hadler-Olsen, A. Schmalfuss, and H. Nermo of the Public Dental Health Service Competence Center of Northern Norway and UiT The Arctic University of Norway, with A-S. Furberg of Molde University College. The authors declared no competing interests.

The authors described it as the first study to assess long-term MIH outcomes beyond age 18. Because MIH was assessed at 16, some affected teeth may already have been restored or extracted, and the number of teeth with severe MIH was small. The authors called for studies with larger cohorts and earlier MIH diagnosis.
